messages:
Priya: Quick run results from this morning — fused vs paged vs flash-attn variants across H100/A100/L40S. Dumping highlights.

Diego: Test matrix: seq=[64,128,256,512,1024,2048], batch=[1,2,4,8,16], models=7B/13B, KV=on/off. Example command we used:
```bash
./bench_attn --model 7B --kernel fused --device h100 --seq 512 --batch 8 --kv-enabled true --repeat 50 --out csv
```
Sample CSV rows (cols: device,kernel,seq,batch,kv,lat_avg_ms,p99_ms,mem_peak_mb):
```
h100,fused,512,8,true,18.5,34.2,16240
 h100,flash,512,8,true,10.3,18.1,14560
 a100,fused,512,8,true,14.2,26.5,15800
 l40s,paged,2048,4,false,95.1,210.7,43000
```

Tomas: Any surprising deltas or regressions? :eyes:

Priya: Yeah — notable: H100 shows ~1.7-1.9x slowdown for fused at seq=512,batch=8 when KV is enabled vs flash. When KV is disabled fused usually wins for short seqs. L40S: paged outperforms fused for seq>=1024 by ~1.3x. A100 sits between.

Ava: Observed memory churn with KV on on H100. nvprof/nvtx shows repeated memcpy + kernel serialization at KV eviction points. First-token latency spike on warm cache looks like page faults / host<->device thrashing.

perf-bot: nvprof summary (trimmed):
```
Time(%)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Name
  42.8   400    0.112   memcpy HtoD (big)
  27.3   400    0.072   fused_attn_kernel_seq512
  18.5   400    0.049   kv_write_coalescer
```

Diego: Hypothesis: fused implementation allocates larger temp workspace for KV ops which can push pressure on HBM and cause host fallbacks. Also pinned memory behaviour on our H100 driver seemed different. Patch we tested toggles workspace prealloc vs on-demand and reduced memcpy by ~20% in microbench.

Priya: Proposed kernel-selection heuristic (draft):
```json
{"policy": "attn_kernel_selection_v2",
 "rules": [
  {"when": "kv_enabled == true and batch * seq >= 4096", "prefer": "flash"},
  {"when": "seq <= 256 and batch <= 8 and kv_enabled == false", "prefer": "fused"},
  {"when": "seq >= 1024", "prefer": "paged"},
  {"fallback": "flash"}
 ]
}
```
(we'll tune thresholds after full sweep)

Tomas: Also add KB warmup: for seq>=512 prepopulate KV cache on cold starts to avoid first-token penalty. Could be a flag in runtime: `--kv-warmup=true` to send synthetic prefix.

Ava: Filed perf regression: https://internal.redwood/perf/2345 with H100 traces + pprof stacks + raw CSVs. (Issue includes workspace snapshots and driver logs).

Diego: Rollout plan: canary 10% with selector attn_kernel_selection_v2; collect p50/p95/p99 token latency, tail mem pressure, and workspace allocation failures. If regression >10% on tail we rollback.

Priya: I'll kick off an H100 follow-up run with the prealloc patch + KV warmup and post updated CSVs in ~30m. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deployed bench cluster job id=bench-2026-03-17-1142-9, artifacts: https://internal.redwood/artifacts/bench-2026-03-17-1142-9/logs.zip

Priya: Follow-up (after run): preliminary: fused improved ~18% with prealloc on H100 but still ~1.15x slower than flash at seq512/b8/kv_on. Next steps: try reducing workspace per-head and/or split KV writes into async batch.

Tomas: Good. Add a short perf test to CI that runs seq=[256,512] batch=[4,8] on a cheap L40S/gpu-emul to catch regressions early.

Ava: Noted. I'll add the CI job and link the perf alert rule to the perf dashboard p99 token latency.

Priya: Great. Closing this thread when CI job + canary are in place.
